newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timorese offer to leave Spanish mission.
newsitem.headline: East Timorese offer to leave Spanish mission.

text.p: Five East Timorese in the Spanish embassy in Jakarta have offered to leave the compound if a statement they have made is broadcast on foreign radio, a human rights activist said on Wednesday.

Johannes Princen, director of the Institute for the Defence of Human Rights, told Reuters he met the five Timorese on Wednesday and they gave him a statement calling for foreign governments to pressure Indonesia on its human rights record.
"They are willing to leave the embassy if their declaration is read on foreign radio," Princen said.
The statement was issued in the name of Hermenegildu Lopes, Valerio Jose Trindade, Amorim Vieira, Marito Dos Santos and Terio Cruz.
Diplomats said some of the men had participated in previous break-ins at the Australian, Dutch and Russian embassies for political reasons rather than seeking asylum.
Deputy mission head Alicia Moral told Reuters on Wednesday the five, who entered on September 10, were still in the embassy in Central Jakarta. She refused to give any more details.
Princen said earlier the five Timorese did not want asylum in Portugal. He would not say what actions they planned upon leaving the embassy.
Princen, a Dutch-born Indonesian national, has acted as a mediator in similar embassy break-ins after which the Timorese have left the missions without leaving the country.

The former Portuguese colony of East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations. The U.N. still regards Portugal as the administering power.
Since September last year, a total of 84 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal after entering foreign embassies in Jakarta.
